title: The Old Man and the Sea
author: Ernest Hemingway
description: 《老人与海》是美国现代文学巨匠欧内斯特·海明威于 1952 年出版的硬汉文学巅峰之作。故事讲述了一位老古巴渔夫圣地亚哥在连续 84 天没打到一条鱼后，单独出海前往墨西哥湾远海。第 85 天，他钓到了一条巨大的马林鱼。经过两天两夜精疲力竭的殊死搏斗，老渔夫克服了饥饿、伤痛与孤独，终于杀死了大鱼。然而在返航途中，大鱼引来了成群鲨鱼的围攻。老渔夫手握残缺的武器，与鲨鱼进行了坚强绝伦的血战，虽然大鱼最终只剩下一具白骨，但圣地亚哥展示了“人可以被毁灭，但不能被打败”的硬汉精神。

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Old Man and the Boy
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 1 章：老渔夫圣地亚哥与忠诚的孩子

paragraphs.en: He was an old man who fished alone in a skiff in the Gulf Stream and he had gone eighty-four days now without taking a fish. In the first forty days a boy had been with him. But after forty days without a fish the boy's parents had told him that the old man was now definitely and finally salao, which is the worst form of unlucky, and the boy had gone at their orders in another boat which caught three good fish the first week.
paragraphs.zh: 他是一位老老人，一个人划着一艘小船在墨西哥湾流中捕鱼，如今他已经连续八十四天没有捕到一条鱼了。在前四十天里，有一个孩子陪着他。但是在四十天没有抓到一条鱼之后，孩子的父母告诉他，老老人现在绝对且最终是“萨拉奥”（也就是最糟糕的倒霉），孩子按照他们的命令去了另一条船，第一周就捕到了三条好鱼。

paragraphs.en: It made the boy sad to see the old man come in each day with his skiff empty and he always went down to help him carry either the coiled lines or the gaff and harpoon and the sail that was furled around the mast. Everything about him was old except his eyes and they were the same color as the sea and were cheerful and undefeated.
paragraphs.zh: 看到老老人每天划着空船回来，孩子感到很难过，他总是跑下去帮他提卷好的钓线，或是携带着搭钩、飞镖和绕在桅杆上的帆。关于他的一切都是古老的，除了他的双眼，它们和大海有着相同的颜色，愉快且未被击败。

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Setting Sail into the Gulf Stream
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 2 章：夜色启航与精确定位

paragraphs.en: Before daylight the next morning, the old man awoke, woke the boy, and ate his breakfast of coffee. Together they carried the gear down to the skiff. The boy wished him good luck, and Santiago rowed out into the dark harbor alone, heading far beyond the other fishing boats into the deep waters of the Gulf Stream. He loved the ocean, thinking of her as la mar, a woman who gives or withholds great favours.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天天亮前，老老人醒来，叫醒了孩子，吃了咖啡早餐。他们一起把用具提到了小船上。孩子祝他好运，圣地亚哥独自划向黑暗的港湾，远远越过其他渔船，驶向墨西哥湾流的深水区。他热爱海洋，把她看作“La Mar”（一位给予或扣留巨大恩惠的女性）。

paragraphs.en: Santiago set his lines with exact precision. Each line was set at a different depth—forty, seventy-five, one hundred, and one hundred and twenty-five fathoms—with fresh sardine bait covering the hooks. 'Every day is a new day,' he thought. 'It is better to be lucky. But I would rather be exact. Then when luck comes you are ready.'
paragraphs.zh: 圣地亚哥极其精确地放下了他的钓线。每条线都设定在不同的深度（四十、七十五、一百和一百二十五英尺），钩子上盖着新鲜的沙丁鱼饵。“每天都是新的一天，”他想。“幸运一点更好。但我宁愿精确。这样当运气来临的时候你已经准备好了。”

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Giant Marlin Strikes
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：巨型马林鱼咬钩

paragraphs.en: Around noon, one of the green hazel sticks dipping into the water leaned sharply forward! Santiago felt the line gently pulled between his thumb and forefinger. He knew instantly that a hundred fathoms down, a giant marlin was nibbling at the sardines covering the point of the hook. He held the line softly, giving the fish plenty of slack to swallow the bait whole.
paragraphs.zh: 正午前后，插在水里的一根绿色榛木棒急剧向前倾斜！圣地亚哥感觉到线在大拇指和食指之间被轻轻拉动。他立刻知道在一百英尺深的底下，一条巨型马林鱼正在啃食盖在钩尖上的沙丁鱼。他软软地握着线，给鱼足够的松弛去把鱼饵整吞下去。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, the line surged taut with colossal weight! Santiago struck with all his strength, driving the hook deep into the marlin's mouth. But the fish did not yield. Instead, the giant marlin began towing the skiff slowly out to sea, heading north-west!
paragraphs.zh: 突然，线带着巨大的重量剧烈拉紧！圣地亚哥用尽全力猛拉，把钩子深深刺入了马林鱼的嘴里。但鱼没有妥协。取而代之的是，巨型马林鱼开始拖着小船向海面缓缓驶去，向西北方向前进！

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Endless Towing in the Night
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：漫长黑夜里的拖曳与坚忍

paragraphs.en: All through the night, the giant marlin towed the skiff seamlessly toward the north. The old man held the line across his back, taking the heavy strain on his shoulders and hands. He was cold, exhausted, and completely alone in the darkness of the sea. 'I wish I had the boy,' he said aloud to the empty ocean.
paragraphs.zh: 整整一个晚上，巨型马林鱼拖着小船无缝地向北驶去。老老人把线背在背上，肩头和双手承受着沉重的拉力。在海洋的黑暗中，他感到寒冷、疲惫且完全孤身一人。“我真希望孩子在这里，”他对着空旷的海洋大声说。

paragraphs.en: When morning broke, his left hand cramped into a tight, useless fist. Pain shot through his back and arms. To maintain his strength, he ate raw tuna without salt. 'Cramps are a treachery of one's own body,' he thought fiercely, willing his cramped left hand to open.
paragraphs.zh: 当清晨破晓时，他的左手抽筋收缩成了一个紧紧的、毫无用处的拳头。痛苦刺穿了他的背部和手臂。为了维持体力，他没有盐吃了生金枪鱼。“抽筋是对自己身体的背叛，”他凶猛地想，用意志强迫他抽筋的左手张开。

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Desperate Battle and the Harpoon Thrust
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：殊死搏斗与飞镖刺杀

paragraphs.en: On the third day, the giant marlin began to circle. Exhausted to the point of blacking out, his eyes dim with fatigue and his hands bleeding, Santiago fought for every inch of line. Each time the fish circled near the skiff, Santiago pulled with all his remaining life.
paragraphs.zh: 在第三天，巨型马林鱼开始转圈。疲惫到了昏厥的边缘，双眼因疲劳而昏暗，双手流着血，圣地亚哥为每寸线而战。每次鱼在小船附近转圈，圣地亚哥都用他仅存的生命去拉。

paragraphs.en: Finally, the marlin came right alongside the boat. Raising his harpoon high above his head, Santiago drove it down with all his strength into the fish's side behind its big chest fin. The marlin rose high out of the water in its death agony, then fell into the sea, floating belly up in a pool of dark crimson blood.
paragraphs.zh: 终于，马林鱼径直来到了船边。将飞镖高高举过头顶，圣地亚哥用尽全力将其向下刺入鱼大胸鳍后面的侧面。马林鱼在临死的痛苦中高高升出水面，然后倒掉进海里，在深暗红色的血泊中腹部朝上漂浮着。

chapters.title: Chapter 6: The First Mako Shark Attack
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 6 章：血腥引诱与首条灰真鲨攻击

paragraphs.en: The old man lashed the giant marlin alongside the skiff, raised his small sail, and turned the boat toward home. But the blood trailing from the fatal wound sank deep into the ocean waters.
paragraphs.zh: 老老人把巨型马林鱼绑在小船边，升起了他的小帆，调转船头回家。但从致命伤口拖出的血痕沉入了大洋水深深处。

paragraphs.en: One hour later, the first Mako shark arrived. It came up fast from the deep water, jaws lined with razor teeth. Santiago waited until the shark closed in, then drove his harpoon deep into its brain! The Mako sank into the abyss, but it took forty pounds of prime meat from the marlin.
paragraphs.zh: 一个小时后，第一条灰真鲨到达了。它从深水区飞快地上升，双颚排列着剃刀牙齿。圣地亚哥等待着直到鲨鱼靠近，然后将他的飞镖深深刺入了它的大脑！灰真鲨沉入了深渊，但它从马林鱼身上带走了四十磅优质的肉。

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Midnight Swarm of Scavengers
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：深夜成群食腐鲨鱼围攻

paragraphs.en: Santiago knew more sharks would come. 'A man can be destroyed but not defeated,' he muttered, resolving to fight to the end. He lashed his knife to an oar, creating a crude spear. He fought off shovel-nosed sharks until his blade snapped.
paragraphs.zh: 圣地亚哥知道更多的鲨鱼会来。“一个人可以被毁灭，但不能被打败，”他自言自语，决心战斗到底。他把刀系在一根桨上做成粗糙的矛。他打退铲鼻鲨直到刀刃折断。

paragraphs.en: As night fell, a pack of scavengers arrived in the dark. Santiago fought blindly with the wooden tiller, bashing their noses until his shoulders ached with agony. But the sharks tore away the rest of the meat until nothing remained except the bare white skeleton.
paragraphs.zh: 当夜晚降临，一群食腐动物在黑暗中到达了。圣地亚哥用木制舵柄盲目地战斗，猛击它们的鼻子直到他的双肩因痛苦而发酸。但鲨鱼撕扯掉剩余的肉，直到除了裸露的白骨外什么也没剩下。

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Home and the Undefeated Spirit
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：重返港湾与永不言败的灵魂（终极结局）

paragraphs.en: In the small hours before dawn, Santiago sailed his skiff into the quiet harbor. He tied the boat to a rock, looking back at the giant eighteen-foot fish skeleton bound to the skiff. Shouldering his mast, he climbed up to his shack and fell asleep on his bed.
paragraphs.zh: 在黎明前的丑时，圣地亚哥划着小船驶入了平静的港湾。他把船系在石头上，回头看着绑在小船上的十八英尺巨型鱼骨。扛着桅杆，他爬上他的小破棚并在床上睡着了。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, the boy came to the shack. Seeing the old man's bloody hands resting in sleep, the boy wept. Fishermen gathered in awe around the skeleton. The boy sat beside Santiago until he awoke, promising: 'We will fish together again.' Santiago smiled gently and closed his eyes to rest, dreaming of the lions.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，孩子来到了小破棚。看到老老人睡梦中沾满鲜血的双手，孩子哭了。渔夫们带着敬畏拥挤在骨架周围。孩子坐在圣地亚哥身边直到他醒来，承诺：“我们还要一起捕鱼。”圣地亚哥温柔地笑了笑，闭上双眼休息，梦见那些狮子。
